Subject: Temporary priority lane request + autoscale exception (regression sweep)

Team —

Quick ask: Brightline (Alice) is running a week-long performance regression sweep across three prod-like clients starting Thursday. They need a predictable, low-jitter slice of dedicated capacity for 48 hours each day of the run (peak window 02:00–10:00 PDT) to reproduce an edge-case latency regression we saw in their production traces.

We'd like to request:
- A temporary priority lane carved out of the east-us GPU pool: ~10 T4-equivalent slots (can be mixed) for Thu–Sat (48h each) starting 2026-06-18 02:00 PDT.
- Autoscale exception: prevent aggressive preemption for that slice during the 02:00–10:00 window; we can accept a soft de-prioritization outside that window.
- Fallback plan: if carving is impossible, permission to route to a quantized variant (gpt-medium-q4) with adjusted headroom and a warm KV-cache snapshot.

I attached a short runbook and Brightline’s traffic projection. Can infra confirm feasibility and any operational impact (SLOs, cost delta) by EOD tomorrow? Kimberly — can product weigh in on rollback/fallback constraints for the experiment?

Thanks,
Olga
Principal Product Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: regression_runbook.pdf (run steps), brightline-mvp-traffic-projection.xlsx (traffic by hour)

On Tue, Jun 16, 2026 at 3:02 PM Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Quick ask: Brightline (Alice) is running a week-long performance regression sweep...

Thanks for the clear ask, Olga. Short answer: probably yes, but we need to trade a few things.

Constraints and notes:
- Pool headroom: east-us has ~120 active T4-equivalent slots under normal load; carving 10 for this slot is feasible if we accept up to a 12% throughput impact for on-demand queues during the 02:00–10:00 window.
- Preemption policy: we can add a temporary tag (priority: brightline-experiment) and set soft-preempt=false for that tag during the run window. This requires an autoscale policy exemption ticket (I’ll create).
- Warm KV: we can snapshot a KV-cache, but restoring it will add ~2–3min cold-start per node; recommend pre-warming 30 minutes prior to each window.
- Cost delta: rough estimate attached in capacity_delta.csv (running estimate: +$1.2k/day).

Operational asks for product/CS:
- We need a rollbackable input: a clear kill switch (ops can revoke the priority tag) and an agreed SLA for Brightline if we see downstream latency regressions.
- Kimberly: are there any product constraints that block using the quantized fallback (gpt-medium-q4) for fidelity comparisons?

I'll open the autoscale exception ticket and tag the nodes. If approved, infra will schedule the carve and provide the node list and IPs.

—Marcus
Infra Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity_delta.csv (daily delta est)

Thanks Marcus — a couple of operational suggestions: 

1) Canary ramp: rather than carving 10 slots immediately, can we stage 4 -> 7 -> 10 across the first three windows? That reduces risk to other customers and makes rollback easier.
2) Observability hooks: add two synthetic transactions that exercise the worst-case prompt patterns from Brightline every 5m so we can detect regressions within the 02:00–10:00 window.
3) Cost sharing: ask Brightline to cover incremental infra cost for the carve (we can credit back if the run is longer). Kimberly — can you own the ask to Brightline?

If we do staged ramps, infra can pre-allocate nodes and mark them with the priority tag; pre-warm can be automated in the runbook.

-Neha

- Procurement: we should ask Brightline to sign a short addendum to their pilot agreement covering extra daily infra ($1.2k/day estimate) and a 2-week rollback window. I can draft and send today.
- SLA/Rollback: agree with Neha on the staged ramp. Also add a condition that if any production SLO for other customers degrades by >5% in the window, ops will auto-revoke the tag.
